subject: Dedicated capacity sizing & SKU allocation approval — Pioneer Health
messages:
From: Aritra Sen <aritra@pioneerhealth.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
Cc: Pioneer Health Procurement <procurement@pioneerhealth.com>
Date: 2026-05-13T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Initial sizing ask — Pioneer MLP dedicated lanes

Hi Irene / Sean,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. Pioneer is getting close to a formal procurement window and procurement asked that we land a recommended reserved-capacity ask for the product team. High-level ask from engineering: sustained ~38k GPU-hours/month for inference (mixed batch/stream), spike tolerance to 65k for 48-hour windows, and the ability to stage activation over 3 months.

Can you provide a proposed reserved SKU allocation + term (12/24/36 months) and the discount breakpoints you would offer? Procurement attached a short template for term sheets (see Pioneer_MLP_commit_term_sheet_v1.pdf).

Also, they asked for any market-index fallback language if GPU market costs materially shift during the term — they flagged risk around long-term GPU pricing volatility.

Would like a short mutual action plan by EOD Friday so they can slot this into their vendor review.

Thanks,
Aritra
Head of ML Ops, Pioneer Health
From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
To: Aritra Sen <aritra@pioneerhealth.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-05-13T13:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Initial sizing ask — Pioneer MLP dedicated lanes

Aritra — thanks for the clarity and the template. Quick summary of what we recommend for Pioneer based on expected Q4 usage patterns and our autoscaling safety margins:

- Recommended reserved allocation: 40 x GPU-equivalent v100/ampere-sim SKU (equivalent to ~38–42k GPU-hours/month with typical utilization).
- Activation plan: phase 1 (month 1) 50% capacity, month 2 75%, month 3 full.
- Term options: 24-month recommended for balance of discount vs. flexibility; we can offer 12-month (lower discount) or 36-month (incremental discount).
- Discount guidance (illustrative): 12m = base price, 24m = 18% discount, 36m = 26% discount. Discounts assume standard sku mix and no unusual burst windows.

On the market-index fallback: we can include an index clause that allows a one-way upward pass-through if an agreed GPU market index moves >18% vs. baseline for a rolling 30-day period. We should draft the exact trigger language — attaching a first pass (GPU_index_clause_draft.docx).

Action items request (Pioneer / Redwood):
1) Pioneer: confirm preferred term (12/24/36) and acceptable phased activation dates.
2) Pioneer: confirm whether the >18% GPU-index trigger is acceptable or if you prefer a symmetric corridor.
3) Redwood (Irene/Marissa): we'll run the discount through Finance for approval and surface any escalation required by Friday.

I'll loop in Finance for approval gates. Sean — do you want me to propose the canary/capacity-swap fallback options as well?

Best,
Irene
Director, Dedicated Capacity — Redwood Inference
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-05-14T10:02:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Initial sizing ask — Pioneer MLP dedicated lanes

Irene / Sean — reviewing the proposed discount tiers. A few internal controls and notes from finance: 

- Discounts >20% require VP Finance sign-off (we can approve up to 22% as a delegated limit with revenue ops confirmation). Anything >22% needs CFO review and written rationale tied to committed ARR.
- We need the SKU mix (weighting between large and small GPU SKUs) to validate cost-to-serve. If Pioneer is mostly long-sequence inference, cost profile increases ~8–12%.
- The GPU market-index clause is acceptable as a concept, but we must limit pass-through to upward adjustments only (no downward refunds) and include a cap per 12-month window (e.g., max pass-through 10% per year).

Please provide a short appendix with: estimated monthly token/unit economics at proposed utilization, and a simple sensitivity table showing Redwood unit margin at -10% / baseline / +15% GPU cost movements. I can then assemble a price-approval memo to support any escalations.

Kimberly Park
Director, Revenue Finance — Redwood Inference
From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Aritra Sen <aritra@pioneerhealth.com>
Date: 2026-05-15T08:19:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Initial sizing ask — Pioneer MLP dedicated lanes

Kim / Irene — thanks. Short ask from Sales: Pioneer is a strategic prospect (healthcare payor) and willing to commit to 24 months at the 18% discount if we can include the phased activation and a capped GPU-index clause. They have a reasonable volume runway and potential for expansion at year 1.

Proposal from Sales for Finance approval: allow up to a 25% structured discount in exchange for the following:
- 24-month firm commit at the recommended reserved allocation (40 GPU-equivalents),
- phased activation as Irene outlined,
- a canary deployment window for month 1 where we provide burst capacity subject to pre-agreed usage spikes (to avoid immediate oversubscription),
- inclusion of the GPU-index upward-only pass-through capped at 10% per 12 months and subject to agreed measurement methodology.

Rationale: closing Pioneer now materially accelerates our mid-market foothold in health vertical and unlocks a reference customer for 2027. If Finance can confirm delegated approval to 25% conditional on a margin sensitivity memo (Kimberly), we will route the term sheet to Pioneer and start DocuSign.

Next steps: Kimberly — can you confirm whether a 25% conditional approval is possible with a signed revenue ops checklist? Marissa — if Finance signs off, can you prepare the routing to Legal/Contracts and set a DocuSign envelope?

—Sean
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: All
Date: 2026-05-18T14:03:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Initial sizing ask — Pioneer MLP dedicated lanes (Approval path)

Team — quick update after review with Rev Ops and Legal. Conditional approval path confirmed with the following guardrails: 

1) Delegated discount ceiling: up to 24% authorized by Revenue Ops + Finance (Kimberly). Anything above 24% requires CFO approval and Exec sponsor note.
2) GPU-index clause: include upward-only pass-through, measurement source = weighted GPU spot index (agreed vendors), trigger >18% for 30-day rolling average, max 10% pass-through per 12 months. Legal will add language to protect Redwood on measurement disputes.
3) Canary/burst: we will honor a 48-hour burst window for the first 30 days (subject to pre-declared windows and a usage guardrail).
4) SKU mix and margin memo: Irene — please deliver the 3-row sensitivity table (Baseline / +15% GPU cost / -10%) and the SKU-weighting detail by tomorrow EOD so Finance can finalize the memo.

Attachments: Pioneer_MLP_commit_term_sheet_v1.pdf (customer template received), GPU_index_clause_draft.docx (first draft).

Once Irene delivers the sensitivity appendix and Duke in Legal signs off on the clause, Marissa will create the DocuSign envelope and push to Aritra for signature.

Action owners: Irene (sensitivity appendix) — due 2026-05-19 EOD; Kimberly (price-approval memo) — due 2026-05-20 noon; Marissa (DocuSign routing) — will queue once the above are in.

Thanks — this gets us to a clean commercial close if Pioneer confirms the 24m commit.

Marissa Cole
Rev Ops — Redwood Inference
